Prod: a ts-node-free path (compiled JS data-source + migration:run/seed scripts) runnable in the slim runtime, wired as a one-shot init service that api depends_on with condition service_completed_successfully. Replaces the host-MySQL, ts-node-only db:setup assumption end-to-end.

tasks.title: Resolve role + regiment + member fresh from DB per request
tasks.summary: Stop trusting role/regiment/member claims baked into the JWT: given only the identity id (sub) from a validated token, resolve the caller's current member (by discordIdentityId), effective role, regimentId and memberId fresh from the DB on each protected request, populating request.user with those live values. Cache the identity->context lookup (following the AuthzService matrix-cache pattern) with an invalidate() hook so role/member changes take effect on the next request without a DB hit per call. This is the enabling layer that makes stale token claims unnecessary and fixes the acceptance-staleness bug (an approved applicant gains Member capabilities on their next request, no re-login).

testPlan.desc: a protected request resolves role/regiment/memberId fresh from DB, not from token claims; changing a member's role in the DB takes effect on the next request with the same token (no re-login)

resolution is cached per identity and invalidated on role/member change; no per-request N+1 DB hit under repeated calls
a token whose identity has no member row resolves as Applicant against the single default regiment (parity with today's identity-only session)

regressionRisk.desc: every protected route depends on this resolver — a bug breaks all authorization, and an uncached lookup adds a DB round-trip to every authenticated request (perf).
regressionRisk.note: Resolver is cached (30s TTL) + explicitly invalidated on role/member/session changes, so no per-request N+1; ban/suspend enforced. Full auth suite + a live /auth/me round-trip pass.

tasks.title: iat-based session invalidation (tokensValidAfter cutoff)
tasks.summary: Leverage the token's issued-at (iat) to validate a token cheaply without a revocation list: add a `sessionsValidFrom` cutoff on discord_identities (new idempotent migration) and reject any token whose iat predates it in JwtStrategy. Bump the cutoff on logout and on sensitive events (ban/suspend, ownership/Discord transfer) so outstanding tokens are invalidated instantly. Accounts for small clock skew.

questions.q: Which events should bump sessionsValidFrom (hard-invalidate outstanding tokens): logout only, or also ban/suspend and ownership/Discord transfer? Recommend logout + ban/suspend + transfers.
questions.answer: do whatever is best practice and secure

testPlan.desc: a token with iat before the identity's sessionsValidFrom is rejected with 401
a normally issued token (iat >= sessionsValidFrom) authenticates as before
logout (and the chosen sensitive events) bump sessionsValidFrom and immediately invalidate previously issued tokens
the migration adds sessionsValidFrom idempotently and db:setup (create -> migrate -> seed) still runs clean

regressionRisk.desc: an incorrect cutoff or clock skew could invalidate every live session at once (mass forced re-login); the comparison and any skew tolerance need care.
regressionRisk.note: Cutoff compared at whole-second granularity with the iat second, avoiding a freshly-issued token being wrongly rejected or a mass invalidation from skew. Unit-tested boundaries.

history.note: created via bf-plan: use the iat timestamp + a per-identity cutoff to validate/invalidate tokens without a revocation list

iat-based session invalidation (sessions_valid_from cutoff) + migration; bumped on logout/ban/suspend; second-granularity comparison avoids skew mass-invalidation. Built + unit/e2e tested (212 unit + 28 e2e green), lint/build clean, adversarially reviewed, and verified end-to-end against a real Discord test guild. Frontend companion shipped in lockstep. tasks.title: Derive guild membership from the bot, not the OAuth guilds scope
tasks.summary: At sign-in, stop calling isMemberOfGuild() (which reads the OAuth `guilds` scope via GET /users/@me/guilds) and instead resolve membership through the already-present bot: guildMember = (await discordGateway.fetchMember(discordUserId)) !== null. Wire DiscordGateway into AuthService/AuthModule and degrade to guildMember=false (never block login) if the bot is unavailable, matching today's fetchGuilds([]-on-failure) behaviour.

testPlan.desc: signing in with a user who IS in the regiment guild sets discord_identities.guild_member = 1 via the bot (no /users/@me/guilds call is made)
signing in with a user who is NOT in the guild sets guild_member = 0
when the bot/gateway is unavailable, sign-in still succeeds and guild_member falls back to 0 (login is never blocked)
member-detail DTO still surfaces guildMember correctly for a roster entry

regressionRisk.desc: AuthService now calls DiscordGateway.fetchMember inline during the synchronous sign-in path; the gateway was previously invoked only by the outbox worker (which isolates failures), so a slow/throwing bot call must not stall or fail login.
regressionRisk.note: Resolved: resolveGuildMembership wraps DiscordGateway.fetchMember in a 4s timeout + try/catch and returns false on any error, so a slow/hung/throwing bot can never stall or fail login (parity with the old fetchGuilds([]-on-failure)). Adversarial review confirmed non-throwing on every failure mode; unit-tested throw + hang branches.
